title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 45: Cale88 seen as small-time despite millions in money flows
summary: The 45th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte began with the Senate impeachment court ordering OVP spokesperson Paolo Panelo to explain his remarks alleging bias by some…

blocks.text: The 45th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte began with the Senate impeachment court ordering OVP spokesperson Paolo Panelo to explain his remarks alleging bias by some senator-judges.
Panelo defended his comments as part of his freedom of speech.

Defense witness and Trade and Industry Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo testified that Cale88 Foods Corp., a listed business interest of the Vice President’s husband, Manases Carpio, is a registered micro, small and medium enterprise.
Likewise, Rodolfo said the firm stopped operations in 2025 due to a change in ownership.
Rodolfo also said that, from 201 employees in 2024, the firm only had 50 workers in 2025 based on its submissions to the Board of Investments under DTI.

At the same time, Rodolfo testified that Cale88 only had zero and two employees in 2024 and 2025, respectively, based on the firm’s General Information Sheet submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The witness said there was no reason for Cale88 Foods Corporation to surpass its declared sales of P208 million in 2022 to 2025.

He made the testimony after senator-judges pointed out that the money inflow and outflow to Cale88 accounts reached P1.2 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions based on the records of the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said it was puzzling that Cale88 did not apply for incentives when it registered before the BOI, which regulates fiscal incentives for firms and considering the billions worth of bank transactions that it recorded under its account.
Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros said it "sounds bananas" that Cale88 was able to produce 422,000 kilos of banana chips in 2025 with only two employees and three officials.

Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Director Pilar Marilyn Pagayunan, meanwhile, testified that Cale88 Foods Corp. was granted product registration documents, or the Certificate of Product Registration.
The FDA official, however, said she won’t be able to testify on the capacity of Cale88 to produce over 400,000 kilos of banana chips.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero asked the defense team if they bought a sample of the banana chips.
Defense counsel Justin Gular, however, said the defense does not have samples of the chips.
Gular said they will present a proper witness who can speak on Cale88’s production.
The impeachment trial will resume on December 1 to give way to the ongoing Senate deliberations on the proposed P7.2 trillion budget for 2027.—LDF, GMA News
